h1: Onix Hotel Bangkok — Clean Rooms, Genuine Value Just 500 m from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital
intro: When a family member needs care at Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital, location matters above everything else — and Onix Hotel Bangkok sits just ~500 metres away, a 4-minute drive. Better still, the hospital sends a complimentary minibus to collect guests from the hotel lobby, removing the stress of arranging taxis in an unfamiliar part of the city. The 4-star property on Rama IX Soi 53 offers 73 rooms clad in onyx marble, a full-service restaurant (Daddy G's Smoke and Brew), a 24-hour bar, free parking and free Wi-Fi. Rates run from approximately ฿900/night in the low season up to around ฿1,400–1,800 during long holidays. Overall guest score: 8.4 from 629 verified reviews on HotelsCombined.

body.html: The detail that separates Onix Hotel Bangkok from every other mid-range option in this neighbourhood is one that no star rating captures: Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital runs a complimentary minibus service directly to the hotel. Multiple guest reviews confirm that a single call to reception is all it takes — the hospital vehicle arrives, collects you, and drops you at the entrance. For patients recovering from procedures, or relatives shuttling back and forth across several days, the value of this cannot be overstated.

The hotel's 73 rooms are spread across four categories. The entry-level Superior Room (28 sqm) comes with a queen or twin configuration, air conditioning, flat-screen TV, mini-fridge, kettle and a marble bathroom. Step up to the Superior with Bathtub (35 sqm) if you need the extra space for longer stays. The Deluxe (35 sqm) and Deluxe Closet (38 sqm) — the latter with a separate dressing room — are the standout choices if budget allows. Trip.com guests scored cleanliness at 9.2 and facilities at 8.8, which is meaningfully above average for a hotel at this price point in Bangkok.

"Clean, comfortable room — and when we needed to go to the hospital, the staff called ahead and the hospital sent a shuttle to pick us up. No taxi drama whatsoever. Staff were kind and genuinely helpful throughout our stay."

Daddy G's Smoke and Brew, the in-house restaurant, serves slow-cooked American smokehouse dishes alongside an international menu and the hotel's own craft beer label — Yaksa Pale Ale. The adjoining bar stays open around the clock, which matters when you're returning from a hospital visit at an unpredictable hour and need a meal. On the third floor, The Playground provides a family relaxation area with a children's zone; the fourth-floor Auditorium is a semi-open garden space used for quiet downtime. Most reviewers describe the atmosphere as calm and suited to recuperation — exactly what this audience needs.

A few points to factor in before booking. Breakfast is not included in the room rate — it can be added at approximately ฿350 per person per day. Most reviews praised the food variety, though a handful mentioned that breakfast-counter staff could be more attentive. Wi-Fi was generally rated fast and reliable. Free parking makes this an unusually practical choice for families driving up from the provinces — a significant share of Samitivej Srinakarin's patient base does exactly that.

The location in Rama IX Soi 53 is residential and quiet — which works in favour of anyone who needs rest, but means you depend on a vehicle for everything beyond the hotel and hospital. The nearest BTS station (Hua Mak on the Yellow Line) is about 1.9 km away — roughly a 10-minute ride share. Seacon Square shopping mall and the area around Srinakarin Road are driveable, but not walkable. There is a 7-Eleven nearby for essentials. Travellers who plan to explore Bangkok's sights and nightlife will find this location inconvenient; it is specifically engineered for the medical-visit demographic.

Putting it plainly: Onix Hotel Bangkok is the most practical base in its price range for anyone tied to Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital. At around ฿900 on a regular night — rising to ฿1,400–1,800 on peak dates — it delivers cleaner, newer-feeling rooms than most competitors at the same price, free parking, a 24-hour restaurant and bar, and a hospital that literally comes to collect you. The only honest trade-offs are the absence of a pool, the extra cost for breakfast, and a location that requires a car for anything unrelated to the hospital.

The trade-offs are an isolated residential location, no pool, and breakfast at extra cost.
honestChecks: If you want to explore Bangkok or shop within walking distance — Rama IX Soi 53 is a quiet residential lane far from the BTS and major malls; you will need a ride-share for every outing → this hotel makes sense only if the hospital is your primary reason for being in this part of the city.

If you need breakfast included in your room rate — it is not; you will pay around ฿350 per person per day extra → check whether a breakfast-inclusive package is available when booking, or budget for nearby local restaurants and 7-Eleven for morning meals.
If a swimming pool is non-negotiable — Onix Hotel Bangkok has no pool → The Xtreme Suites, roughly 1.4 km away and also close to the hospital, is an alternative worth comparing.

tips.title: Ask Reception to Arrange the Hospital Shuttle
tips.body: Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital provides a free minibus pickup from the hotel — tell the front desk staff your appointment time in advance so they can coordinate with the hospital's transport team. No need to hail a taxi.

tips.title: Drive In — Parking Is Free
tips.body: In-hotel parking is complimentary, a genuine rarity in Bangkok. If you are driving from another province, this alone saves a meaningful amount over several nights. Confirm availability during long Thai holidays when occupancy spikes.

tips.title: Budget for Breakfast Separately
tips.body: Breakfast is not in the room rate (approx. ฿350/person/day at Daddy G's). If you prefer cheaper options, there is a 7-Eleven nearby and local rice-soup shops in the surrounding lanes — good for early hospital-day mornings.

tips.title: Use the Yellow Line BTS for City Access
tips.body: Hua Mak station (BTS Yellow Line) is about 1.9 km away — a 10-minute ride share. From there you can reach Central Rama 9, Terminal 21 and the rest of Bangkok without fighting traffic. Factor this in if you want flexibility beyond hospital visits.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Onix Hotel Bangkok

faq.q: How far is Onix Hotel Bangkok from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is approximately 500 metres from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital — a 4-minute drive. Crucially, the hospital itself operates a complimentary minibus that picks up guests directly from the hotel lobby. Just let the front desk know your appointment time and they will coordinate with the hospital's transport team.

faq.q: What are the room types and prices at Onix Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: There are four room categories: Superior (28 sqm, from approx. ฿900), Superior with Bathtub (35 sqm), Deluxe (35 sqm) and Deluxe Closet (38 sqm with separate dressing room, from approx. ฿1,400). Rates rise to around ฿1,400–1,800 during Thai long-holiday weekends. Always compare across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com for the best rate.

faq.q: Does Onix Hotel Bangkok have free parking?
faq.a: Yes, parking is complimentary — making this an unusually practical choice for families driving from other provinces to use Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital. Confirm availability when booking during peak periods.

faq.q: Is breakfast included at Onix Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: Breakfast is not included in the standard room rate. It can be added at the in-house Daddy G's Smoke and Brew restaurant for approximately ฿350 per person per day. Some booking packages include breakfast — check at time of reservation. Alternatively, a 7-Eleven and local rice-soup shops are within walking distance for lighter, cheaper breakfasts.

faq.q: Is Onix Hotel Bangkok easy to reach by public transport?
faq.a: Not particularly. The nearest BTS station is Hua Mak (Yellow Line), about 1.9 km away — a 10-minute ride-share. This hotel is best suited to guests with a private car or those who will primarily move between the hotel and the hospital. For city-wide exploration, budget for ride-shares to the BTS or MRT network.
